title: Annotating metabolic enzymes in parasitic worm proteomes
protocol: Use BRENDA for predicting ECs.
Map sequences from SWISSPROT annotated with EC numbers in BRENDA to sequences in the genome via a two-way reciprocal BLAST-based search strategy.
Use DETECT v1.0 to predict ECs.
Apply a high confidence cutoff ILS of 0.9 (inclusive) requiring at least 5 positive matches.
Include hits with ILS > 0.2 where sequences are annotated with the same EC in DETECT and BLAST against SWISSPROT database.
Retain discordant ECs if they have a higher E-value in BLAST (>1e-30), differing either by EC or only in the fourth digit of the classification hierarchy.
Use PRIAM to predict ECs.
Set minimum probability > 0.5, profile coverage > 70%, and check catalytic - TRUE.
Use KAAS (KEGG Automatic Annotation Server) to predict ECs.
Utilize a locally installed version 2 of KAAS with default settings (bi-directional best hit with bit-score threshold of 35).
Associate KOs annotated by KAAS with corresponding ECs using KO and EC definitions in KEGGv70.
Find the ECs common between predictions of PRIAM and KAAS for each species.
Call this set of ECs “EC_set_1”.
Combine the ECs obtained using BRENDA and DETECT with EC_set_1 for each species.
Run Pathway Tools pipeline for each species using "EC set A" as input.
Assign evidence scores for pathway predictions based on presence of most ECs for a pathway.
Assign evidence scores based on presence of unique ECs.
Assign evidence scores based on presence of the first two steps for degradation pathways.
Assign evidence scores based on presence of the last two steps for biosynthetic pathways.
Assign evidence scores if more than 50% enzymes are present for energy metabolism pathways.
Use taxonomic pruning to reduce false-positives wherever information is available.
Remove KEGG pathways that aren’t relevant to helminths by including only those with at least one reference pathway for a nematode or platyhelminth species in the KEGG database.
Exclude pathways such as ‘Carbon fixation in photosynthetic organisms’ even if some enzymes are found in helminths.
Manually curate and exclude pathways deemed unlikely to be relevant, like caffeine metabolism for C. elegans and C. briggsae.
Use the pathway hole-filler component of Pathway Tools with default settings to assign genes to pathway holes for helminth-relevant KEGG pathways.
Include predictions for genes that either had no assigned ECs or were assigned a different EC but supported by KAAS, PRIAM, or EFICAz v2.5 predictions.
Combine the ECs obtained from step 4 with “EC set A” to yield “EC set B”.
From the helminth species analyzed, identify a set of “Tier 1” species whose genomes and gene models are deemed to have high quality.
Remove Compara gene families that have different ECs assigned after Step B to at least 2 genes from Tier 1 species.
Remove Compara gene families that have less than 2 genes from Tier 1 species annotated with an EC after Step B.
Assign the unique EC to any genes in the remaining Compara gene family without EC annotation after Step B.
Generate a new set of ECs for each species, which is the “EC set C”.
